sources.note: The 2026 OAS-AUWCL Scholarship Program Announcement, an 8-page PDF published by the OAS General Secretariat on oas.org (the awarding body's own domain). Read in full on 12 October 2026.

awarding_body.detail: The page is the OAS General Secretariat's own announcement for a scholarship jointly run with American University Washington College of Law (AUWCL); selection is made jointly by both bodies.
awarding_body.quote: The OAS General Secretariat (GS/OAS) is the central and permanent organ of the Organization of American States (OAS). ... AUWCL and the OAS will select the scholarship awardees, based on the criteria listed above.

deadline.detail: The page publishes two deadlines per intake. As of today (12 October 2026) the Fall 2026 deadlines (May 1 / June 1, 2026) have passed, so the currently open cycle is Spring 2027: Residential LL.M. deadline 1 November 2026 and Hybrid/Online LL.M. deadline 30 November 2026. This matches the record's deadline_label and deadline_date (2026-11-01) exactly. The same deadlines apply to both the Human Rights/HL and the Arbitration & Business Law LL.M. programmes.
deadline.quote: DEADLINES: Admission through AUWCL and scholarship application: Fall 2026: Residential LL.M. - May 1, 2026 Hybrid/Online LL.M. - June 1, 2026 Spring 2027: Residential LL.M. - November 1, 2026 Hybrid/Online LL.M. - November 30, 2026

eligibility.detail: All distinct record claims were confirmed: citizenship/permanent residency of an active OAS member state except the United States; a JD from an ABA-accredited US law school or an equivalent first law degree from a foreign law school; admission to one of the AUWCL LL.M. programmes; open to new applicants and current AUWCL students; ineligibility of current OAS scholarship holders, GS/OAS staff and consultants, and OAS Permanent officials and their immediate relatives. The page adds one requirement the record does not mention: applicants from Argentina must file a required form via the National Liaison Office (ONE).
eligibility.quote: Be a citizen and/or permanent legal resident of any active OAS member state, except the United States. ... Applicants must hold a Juris Doctor (JD) from a US law school accredited by the American Bar Association (ABA) or a first degree in law from a foreign law school with equivalent standards. ... Be admitted to one of the LL.M programs offered by AUWCL ... This scholarship opportunity is open to new applicants as well as current AUWCL students from an OAS member state, except the United States, and who are not a current OAS scholarship recipient. ... Ineligible: Current OAS scholarship holders and Citizens and/or permanent residents of the United States; GS/OAS staff and their immediate relatives or GS/OAS consultants; OAS Permanent officials and their immediate relatives.

funding.detail: The award is a partial tuition waiver - 50% of tuition only. It is correctly recorded as 'Tuition Fee Waiver' and not 'Fully Funded'. Recipients must pay the remaining 50% of tuition (USD 30,972 of a USD 61,944 total) plus travel, mandatory university fees, books, health insurance, graduation and visa costs.
funding.quote: BENEFITS: 50% Tuition waiver ... Remaining 50% of tuition fees; Travel expenses (to and from the country of study), if applicable; Mandatory university fees; Cost of books and study materials; Health insurance; Graduation expenses; Visa expenses (where applicable); and any other costs or additional living and study cost not covered by the scholarship.

degree_levels.detail: All programmes on the page are LL.M. (Master of Laws) degrees - Master's level, as recorded. Three programmes are offered: LL.M. in International Human Rights and Humanitarian Law (English, onsite/hybrid/online), LL.M. en Derechos Humanos y Derecho Humanitario (Spanish, hybrid/online), and LL.M. in International Arbitration and Business Law (English, onsite/hybrid/online).
degree_levels.quote: PROGRAMS: LL.M in International Human Rights and Humanitarian Law; LL.M. en Derechos Humanos y Derecho Humanitario; LL.M. in International Arbitration and Business Law

recommended_field_updates.deadline_text: Spring 2027: Residential LL.M. - November 1, 2026; Hybrid/Online LL.M. - November 30, 2026 (Fall 2026 deadlines of May 1 / June 1, 2026 had already passed on the check date)
recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: Read in full on 12 Oct 2026 from the OAS PDF announcement. Award is a 50% tuition waiver only (USD 30,972 of USD 61,944 tuition remains the scholar's cost, plus fees/travel/insurance/visa) - never label this Fully Funded. Applies to three AUWCL LL.M. programmes with identical deadlines. Applications must first be admitted by AUWCL. Awardees are published in August and December at www.oas.org/scholarships. Argentina applicants need the DGCIN nota via the National Liaison Office. Recipients must commit to return to their sponsoring OAS member state for the length of the scholarship. Re-check before 1 Nov 2026 for the Spring 2028 cycle deadlines.

notes_for_reviewer: No conflicts found; every record claim was confirmed verbatim from the official PDF. Two things a human should know before trusting the card: (1) the funding is a 50% tuition waiver with substantial out-of-pocket costs (remaining tuition USD 30,972 plus mandatory fees, travel, insurance, books, visa), so it must not be presented as a full scholarship; (2) the announcement also covers two other AUWCL LL.M. programmes (Spanish-language HRHL and International Arbitration and Business Law) under the same deadlines, so the record's coverage of 'the AUWCL LL.M.' generally is accurate but the catalogue does not name the three specific programmes.
